question: Dakshinchitra was compiled during the reign of which Pallava ruler?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Mahendravarman I**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• **Dakshinchitra** is an ancient treatise or a commentary on the art of **painting** that provides insights into the aesthetic traditions of early **South India**.

• The work was compiled under the royal patronage of the **Pallava** ruler **Mahendravarman I**, who reigned from approximately **600 to 630 CE**.

• **Mahendravarman I** was a great scholar and artist, often referred to by the title **Chitrakarapuli** (Tiger among painters) due to his profound mastery and promotion of the fine arts.

• He was also known as **Vichitrachitta** (Curious-minded), reflecting his innovative approach to temple architecture, specifically the introduction of **rock-cut temples** in the **Tamil** country, such as the **Mandagapattu** temple.

• His interest in documentation and theory led to the compilation of **Dakshinchitra**, which served as a significant reference for the **Pallava** style of mural painting, remnants of which can be found in **Sittannavasal**.

 **Additional Information__**

• **Narasimhavarman I**:

• He was the son and successor of **Mahendravarman I**, famously known as **Mamalla** (the great wrestler).

• He is credited with the creation of the monolithic **Rathas** and the shore temple complex at **Mahabalipuram**.

• He achieved a major military victory over the **Chalukya** king **Pulakeshin II**, earning the title **Vatapikonda**.

• **Sivaskandavarman**:

• He was an early ruler of the **Pallava Dynasty** during the 4th century CE.

• He is known from the **Hirahadagalli** and **Mayidavolu** inscriptions and is recognized for performing **Vedic** sacrifices like the **Ashvamedha**.

• **Vijayaskandavarman**:

• Another early **Pallava** monarch who contributed to the consolidation of the kingdom before the rise of the **Imperial Pallavas**.
